brief.t: Tata Capital is the main lending company of the Tata group (a subsidiary of Tata Sons). It gives loans to individuals, small businesses (SMEs) and large companies, and owns Tata Capital Housing Finance.
Tata Motors Finance (vehicle loans for Tata trucks and cars) merged into Tata Capital; the merger became effective on 8 May 2025, and Tata Motors got shares in Tata Capital.
Listed on NSE and BSE on 13 October 2025 after a ₹15,512 crore IPO at ₹326 a share, the biggest ever IPO by an Indian NBFC. RBI rules made it list because it is an 'upper layer' NBFC.
FY 2025-26 profit (owners' share, consolidated) rose about 32% to ₹4,846 crore; AUM reached ₹2.77 lakh crore.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026): profit ₹1,660 crore, up 51%; AUM crossed ₹3 lakh crore at ₹3,08,030 crore.

timeline.t: Tata Capital started as the Tata group's financial services company.
Rajiv Sabharwal (ex-ICICI Bank) took over as MD & CEO from Praveen Kadle.
Tata Motors Finance merged into Tata Capital, adding vehicle loans.
₹15,512 crore IPO; shares listed on NSE and BSE on 13 October.
Kamal Bhatia became Chief Risk Officer, succeeding Nitin Dharma.

model.how: Tata Capital borrows money from banks and bond investors, and lends it out as personal, home, vehicle, business and corporate loans. It earns the gap between the interest it charges and what it pays, plus fees.
flow: Borrows from banks and bond markets
Lends to people, SMEs and companies

points: RBI puts the biggest NBFCs in an 'upper layer' with bank-like rules; they must list on the stock market, which is why Tata Capital did its IPO in 2025.
NBFCs borrow from banks and bond markets, so their cost of funds and credit rating matter a lot.
Big theme for interviews: using AI and digital journeys to give loans faster and keep bad loans low.

glossary.NBFC: Non-Banking Financial Company: a lender regulated by the RBI that gives loans but cannot take savings or current account deposits like a bank.
glossary.AUM: Assets Under Management: the total loans an NBFC has given out and not yet been repaid. The main size measure for a lender.
glossary.Disbursements: New loans paid out to customers in a period.
glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on borrowings. A lender's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of loans or interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Loans not repaid for 90+ days (called 'Stage 3' loans by NBFCs), as a % of all loans.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.Stage 3 assets: Loans that have stopped paying for 90+ days. NBFCs report Gross and Net Stage 3, similar to banks' NPA.
glossary.Credit cost: Money set aside for bad loans, as a % of average loans. Lower means fewer losses.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The lender's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires NBFCs to keep at least 15%.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Borrowings: Money an NBFC raises from banks, bonds (NCDs), commercial paper and, for some, public deposits, to lend onward.
glossary.Cost of funds: The average interest an NBFC pays on its borrowings. NBFCs usually pay more than banks, so a strong credit rating matters.
glossary.Credit rating: An agency's grade (e.g. AAA) of how safely a company can repay debt. Higher ratings mean cheaper borrowing.
glossary.Upper Layer NBFC: The largest and most important NBFCs, named by the RBI under its scale-based rules. They face bank-like rules and must list on the stock market within 3 years.
glossary.Return on assets: Net profit as a % of average total assets. Shows how well a lender earns on what it owns.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates banks and NBFCs in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before giving a loan.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that lenders serve.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like insurance or a second loan) to an existing customer.
glossary.Co-lending: A bank and an NBFC lending together: the NBFC finds and services the borrower, the bank funds most of the loan.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Net total income: Net Interest Income plus fees and other income. Tata Capital reports this as its main 'top line'.
glossary.Cost-to-income ratio: Operating costs as a % of net income. Lower means the lender runs more efficiently.
glossary.Motor finance: Loans for buying trucks, buses and cars. Tata Capital got this business by merging Tata Motors Finance in 2025.
glossary.Offer for sale: In an IPO, existing shareholders sell some of their shares; the money goes to them, not the company.
glossary.Owners' share of profit: The part of group profit that belongs to the company's own shareholders, after removing the share of minority owners in subsidiaries.

Role knowledge, the company and HR questions

Finance.q: Why did Tata Capital have to list on the stock market?
Finance.a: RBI places the largest NBFCs in an 'upper layer' and requires them to list. Tata Capital did a ₹15,512 crore IPO and listed on 13 October 2025.

Finance.q: Why is Q2 FY27 profit shown as ₹1,660 cr in some places and ₹1,832 cr in others?
Finance.a: ₹1,660 cr is the profit belonging to Tata Capital's own shareholders. ₹1,832 cr is total consolidated profit, which also includes the share of minority owners in subsidiaries. Always say which figure you mean.

Finance.q: What does Gross Stage 3 of 1.9% mean?
Finance.a: About 1.9% of loans had stopped paying for 90+ days at September 2026. Lower is better.

Marketing.q: How would you sell a Tata Capital personal loan to a young professional?
Marketing.a: Lead with the Tata trust factor, quick digital approval and clear EMIs; target salaried users through apps and employer tie-ups.

Marketing.q: How can Tata Capital use the Tata Motors Finance customer base?
Marketing.a: Cross-sell insurance, personal and business loans to truck and car owners who already repay vehicle loans.

HR.q: Tata Capital is growing loans 20%+ a year. What is the HR challenge?
HR.a: Hiring and training branch, sales and credit staff fast while keeping turnover low and keeping the Tata culture of trust.

Sales.q: Sell me a business loan for a small shop owner.
Sales.a: Ask about his needs (stock, expansion), show the EMI against his monthly sales, explain fast approval and the Tata name, and close with simple documents.

Operations.q: How does AI help Tata Capital's operations?
Operations.a: AI-assisted checks cover 95%+ of personal and business loan cases, which speeds up approvals and lowers errors and costs.

Other.a: It is the Tata group's NBFC: it lends to individuals, small businesses and companies, and owns Tata Capital Housing Finance.

gd.t: Should every large NBFC be forced to list on the stock market?
gd.for: More transparency, public scrutiny and easier access to capital.
gd.against: Listing adds cost and short-term share-price pressure; RBI rules can already control risk.

gd.for: AI already handles most retail credit checks faster and cheaper.
gd.against: Complex SME and corporate loans still need human judgement and relationships.

avoid: Calling Tata Capital a bank: it is an NBFC and cannot take savings deposits.
Mixing up profit figures: say ₹1,660 cr (owners' share) for Q2 FY27, not ₹1,832 cr, unless you explain the difference.
Confusing Tata Capital with Tata Sons or Tata Motors.
